text.content:
Here you'll find specific instances where rules differ from the main system when you're playing with the Digimon Expansion Module.

The Attribute Triangle

This is a pretty fundamental aspect of Digimon but each Digimon creature will possess one of the following traits;

Vaccine: These creatures gain +50% damage vs Virus Creatures, and inflict 50% less damage vs Data Creatures.

Data: These creatures gain +50% damage vs Vaccine Creatures, and inflict 50% less damage vs Virus Creatures.

Virus: These creatures gain 50% damage vs Data creatures, and inflict 50% less damage vs Vaccine creatures.

Free: These creatures exist outside of the Attribute Triangle and thus have no interaction with it.

All of these traits are automated.

Digivolution

Digivolution is done via the Perk Web, specifically under the Species Tab. Due to the nature of how Digivolution works, it is only practical to do it during downtime.

When you digivolve, you need to consult your new Species and determine if your available abilities have changed. Then, delete old abilities as necessary and reset your new ones. When you make an update to your sheet after Digivolving, it should add your species' Signature Move(s) to your Known Attacks List.

Because of how Digimon retain all non-Signature Move attacks from their prior evolutions, you can only Digivolve 1 Digimon per downtime sequence, and that Digimon may only Digivolve 1 time. This serves to prevent players from yo-yoing around the Digivolution web picking up every attack possible.

Module-Specific Afflictions

Amped

The user's next attack deals +100% Damage.

Felt Made

The Afflicted creature has +4 default EVA Stages, +1 default DEF, SPDEF, and SPD Stage, and +20% RES. Each time the user is hit by a Physical- or Special-Category Attack, the Afflicted creature has a 50% chance of losing -1 EVA Stage for 3 Activations. When this effect expires, the user loses -1 DEF, SPDEF, and SPD Stage for 5 Activations and is @Affliction[delay 50]. This on-expire effect does not occur automatically.

Monkey Wrench

This affliction gives the user -2 to the following Combat Stages: ATK, DEF, SPA, SPD, SPE.

Skill Discs and Attach Skills

Skill Discs are equipment which temporarily grant you new Known Attacks when equipped. They are slotless, so there is no limit on the number you can equip. Unequipping these items removes the associated attack from your Known Attacks. Do make sure to equip them rather than just dragging the associated move to your sheet.

GM Advice

This section will be expanded over time if more tips and tricks are learned.

For significant Digimon enemies, GMs should consider generating them as Fresh or In-Training Digimon of the appropriate level, and then manually digivolving them through the web to ensure they pick up all associated moves for the digivolution path in question. This will help make each mon feel a little different.

If you need to get creatures ready for use in a hurry, don't be afraid to just throw skill discs on them to pad out their arsenal.

Consider pre-baking encounters where possible. Due to the nature of how Digimon work, they're a little harder to generate on the fly, especially at higher generations.

Digimon can, in theory, be most readily played in 3 formats. You can run it as a standard pokemon-trainer style creature catcher setup, or in a more traditional Digimon anime format you can play in the manner of a Digidestined by having 1 tamer, and 1 [Ace] Digimon. Finally, it should be entirely possible to play a "Digimon World" game wherein the players themselves are their chosen Digimon. Maybe you'll come up with other interesting ways to play using this expansion.
